items.stem: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which is always the customer's responsibility?

options.text: Configuring their own IAM permissions and securing their data
options.rationale: Correct: customers are responsible for security 'in' the cloud, including access and data.

options.text: The physical security of AWS data centers

options.rationale: The underlying hardware is AWS's responsibility.

items.explanation: Correct: customers are responsible for security 'in' the cloud, including access and data.

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve the availability of a workload on AWS? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: spreading across AZs survives a single-AZ failure.

options.text: Use managed multi-AZ databases where appropriate
options.rationale: Correct: multi-AZ databases add failover resilience.

options.text: Run everything in a single AZ to reduce latency
options.rationale: A single AZ is a single point of failure.

options.text: Avoid backups to save storage cost

items.explanation: Correct: multi-AZ deployment and managed multi-AZ databases improve availability.

items.stem: An application running on EC2 needs to read from an S3 bucket. What is the recommended way to grant access?

options.text: Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance with least-privilege permissions
options.rationale: Correct: instance roles avoid long-lived keys and follow least privilege.

options.text: Embed root account access keys in the app
options.rationale: Using root keys is insecure and over-privileged.

options.text: Make the bucket public to everyone
Share one IAM user's password with the app
options.rationale: Sharing user passwords is insecure and not how apps authenticate.

items.explanation: Correct: instance roles avoid long-lived keys and follow least privilege.
